findings.standard: An Instar Agent Is Always a Multi-Machine Entity
findings.reason: An older installed peer can acknowledge a chat while discarding the creation context needed to show its parent, leaving that peer unable to reproduce the hierarchy on its own without the durable receipts and catch-up required by the Conversations Pending exception.

findings.standard: Maturation Path — Test Agent → Development Agent → Fleet
findings.reason: The fleet rollout follows native-conversation enablement and the standard release once build and test checks pass, without requiring a graduation decision based on observed development-agent behavior and two independent readings before changing the fleet default.

findings.standard: Observability — you can't tune what you can't see
findings.reason: The verification plan tests individual cases but provides no deployed measure of how often generated chats appear under their verified parent or remain unplaced, even though both outcomes are observable without guessing how much legacy context was lost.

The draft relies on terms such as “Chief,” “team/MSP,” and “exact-head throughput gate” without explaining who controls placement, which readers are excluded, or what evidence clears the release gate.
